title: The $L^2$-weight of a punctually pure lisse sheaf equals its weight
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over
$k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and let $\mathcal G$ be a nonzero lisse Weil sheaf
on $X_0$, punctually
$\iota$-pure of weight $w$. Then, in the $L^2$-weight parameter
$\|\cdot\|$ of [def-wf-l2-norm],

$$
\|\mathcal G\|=w .
$$

Thus the $L^2$-rigidity [thm-wf-l2-dictionary] does not in fact
need its hypothesis of $\iota$-reality: punctual purity of the weight
alone suffices, and in particular the rigidity applies to the
$\iota$-realizable sheaves of
[def-wf-iota-real].

proof.text: Choose $b=\iota^{-1}(q^{-w/2})$ and put $\mathcal G^0=\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal B_b$ as in [def-wf-normalized-real-envelope]. Here $q>1$, so $b\ne0$ and $2\log_q|\iota(b)|=-w$. Applying [lem-wf-constant-twist-weight] with $c=-w$ gives punctual purity of $\mathcal G^0$ of weight $0$. The twist is lisse: on a common local trivialization it is the tensor product of a locally constant finite-rank sheaf and the rank-one locally constant line [def-wf-constant-weil-twist]. It is nonzero, since twisting again by $\mathcal B_{b^{-1}}$ recovers $\mathcal G$ (the scalar characters multiply to $1$).

Write $S_m(\mathcal H)=\|f_{\mathcal H}\|_m^2$. By [lem-wf-trace-energy-constant-twist], $S_m(\mathcal G^0)=q^{-mw}S_m(\mathcal G)$ for every $m\ge1$. Thus, for every real $\beta$, the defining sequence for $\mathcal G^0$ at $\beta$ equals that for $\mathcal G$ at $\beta+w$, since $q^{-mw}/q^{m(\beta+1)}=1/q^{m(\beta+w+1)}$. If $A_{\mathcal H}$ denotes the set of parameters with positive limsup in [def-wf-l2-norm], then $A_{\mathcal G^0}=A_{\mathcal G}-w$. Translation preserves order and suprema in the extended reals: an upper bound $u$ for the translated set corresponds exactly to the upper bound $u+w$ for the original set. This also covers the empty and unbounded sets. Consequently $\|\mathcal G^0\|=\|\mathcal G\|-w$.

source.place: Step 1, equality of energies and translation of the defining parameter set

proof.text: Put $\mathcal E=\mathcal G^0\oplus(\mathcal G^0)^\vee$ as in [def-wf-normalized-real-envelope]. By [lem-tw-dual-negation] applied at weight $0$, the second summand is punctually pure of weight $0$. At each closed point the Frobenius on the direct sum is block diagonal, so its characteristic polynomial is the product of those of the two summands. All its eigenvalues therefore have absolute value $1$; this is punctual purity of weight $0$ by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. The first summand is nonzero, so $\mathcal E$ is nonzero (its inclusion has a left inverse, the projection).

source.place: Step 2, purity and nonvanishing of the envelope

proof.text: By [lem-wf-envelope-real], $\mathcal E$ is lisse and $\iota$-real. It is nonzero and punctually pure of weight $0$ by the preceding step. The base remains the given smooth geometrically connected affine curve, so every hypothesis of [thm-wf-l2-dictionary] holds and it gives $\|\mathcal E\|=0$.

source.place: Step 2, application of the real-sheaf dictionary at weight zero

proof.text: The energy comparison [lem-wf-trace-energy-real-envelope-bound] gives $0\le S_m(\mathcal E)\le4S_m(\mathcal G^0)$ for all $m\ge1$. Divide by the positive number $q^{m(\beta+1)}$. For these nonnegative sequences, if the limsup for $\mathcal G^0$ is zero, then its terms tend to zero: for every $\epsilon>0$ the tail is eventually less than $\epsilon/4$. The comparison then makes the envelope's terms eventually less than $\epsilon$, so its limsup is also zero. Contrapositively every parameter with positive limsup for $\mathcal E$ also has positive limsup for $\mathcal G^0$. Taking the suprema of these nested parameter sets in [def-wf-l2-norm] gives $0=\|\mathcal E\|\le\|\mathcal G^0\|$. This uses only the stated energy inequality, not any assertion from the proof of the reality lemma.

source.place: Step 3, positive-limsup parameter inclusion from the energy comparison

proof.text: A sheaf punctually pure of weight $0$ is mixed of weights at most $0$: the filtration $0\subset\mathcal G^0$ has its only quotient pure of weight $0$, as required by [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Hence [lem-wf-l2-upper] applies to the lisse twist on the same affine curve and gives $\|\mathcal G^0\|\le0$. Together with the previous inequality this proves $\|\mathcal G^0\|=0$.

source.place: Final paragraph, upper bound for the normalized twist

proof.text: The translation identity of step 2 and $\|\mathcal G^0\|=0$ yield $\|\mathcal G\|-w=0$. Translation by the finite real number $w$ is invertible even on the extended reals, so $\|\mathcal G\|=w$. The proof made no reality assumption on $\mathcal G$; therefore the same conclusion holds in particular for the $\iota$-realizable sheaves mentioned in the statement.

source.place: Final paragraph, cancellation of the finite weight shift

proof_origin.place: Opening normalization and Steps 1-3, with explicit parameter-set translation and comparison
